title: Evaluation and reduction equations for the actual exceptional tower mate
statement:
Fix the global datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$ for $n\geq1$. All schemes are separated finite-type $k$-schemes and all maps are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Write $\mathcal C_T=\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$ for the ordinary derived category of strict varying-coefficient towers restricted to constructible levels with common finite cohomological and Tor intervals [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]. Write $r^D_{n,m}:D_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m\to D_m$ for its derived reduction map, $m\leq n$ [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]; normalized means all these maps are invertible.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], let $v:Y'\to Y$ be arbitrary, and put $X'=X\times_Y Y'$ with projections $u:X'\to X$, $f':X'\to Y'$. Fix a compactification $f=pj$ and its pullback for $f'$ [def-cbc-compact-support-square]. Write $F_f=Rf_{!,\bullet}$, $G_f=f^!_\bullet$, and similarly $F_{f'},G_{f'}$, for the tower operations and adjunctions of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels, det-sp-tower-gluing]. Their units and counits are $\eta_f,\varepsilon_f$ and $\eta_{f'},\varepsilon_{f'}$.

Let $\beta:v_\bullet^*F_f\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{f'}u_\bullet^*$ be the actual compactification exchange of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](2b). This exchange restricts to the categories $\mathcal C_X\to\mathcal C_{Y'}$, and its evaluation is the finite compact-support exchange $\beta_n$. For $K\in\mathcal C_Y$ put
$$P_K=u_\bullet^*G_fK,\quad Q_K=G_{f'}v_\bullet^*K,\quad q_K=v_\bullet^*(\varepsilon_{f,K})\circ\beta(G_fK)^{-1}.$$
The actual adjoint transpose $e_K:P_K\to Q_K$, defined by
$$e_K=G_{f'}(q_K)\circ\eta_{f',P_K},$$
is natural in $K$. Its evaluated map is
$$e_{n,K_n}=G_{f',n}(v_n^*\varepsilon_{f,n,K_n}\circ\beta_n(G_{f,n}K_n)^{-1})\circ\eta_{f',n,u_n^*G_{f,n}K_n},$$
where the comparisons of [det-sp-tower-gluing](3) identify evaluated units and counits with finite ones. No invertibility of $e_K$ is assumed or asserted here.

For $T_{nm}=-\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m$, $r=r^K_{n,m}$, and the coefficient comparisons $c^f_{n,m},c^{f'}_{n,m}$ of [det-sp-reduction-exceptional], the source and target reductions, under the canonical tensor/pullback identifications, satisfy
$$r^P_{n,m}=u_m^*G_{f,m}(r)\circ u_m^*c^f_{n,m}(K_n),\qquad r^Q_{n,m}=G_{f',m}(v_m^*r)\circ c^{f'}_{n,m}(v_n^*K_n).$$
The mixed identity of [det-sp-mixed-base-change] for $A_n\to A_m$ gives the following equality, natural in the entire tower $K$, including nonflat coefficient quotients:
$$\begin{aligned}
r^Q_{n,m}\circ T_{nm}(e_{n,K_n})
&=G_{f',m}(v_m^*r)\circ e_{m,T_{nm}K_n}\circ u_m^*c^f_{n,m}(K_n)\\
&=e_{m,K_m}\circ u_m^*G_{f,m}(r)\circ u_m^*c^f_{n,m}(K_n)
=e_{m,K_m}\circ r^P_{n,m}.
\end{aligned}$$
Here all source and target objects lie in the uniform constructible finite-Tor categories; the equality concerns reductions of the already constructed actual tower morphism.

source.place: Proof (1), restriction of compactification exchange; (2), actual transpose, finite evaluation and mixed reduction square

proof.text: First check the domain of the actual exchange. By [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](1), $f'$ is smooth of pure relative dimension $d$; [def-cbc-compact-support-square] supplies the pulled-back compactification. By [lem-sp-ctf-tower-pullback-reconstruction], every object of $\mathcal C_T$ is bounded below, has finite etale-origin evaluations, and its pullbacks stay in $\mathcal C$. For a tower with common Tor interval $[a,b]$, [det-sp-tower-bound-uniform] puts both $F_f$ and $F_{f'}$ in common Tor and cohomological interval $[a,b+2d]$; the geometric fibres have dimension $d$. Thus both sides of $\beta$ preserve the stated subcategories. Apply [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](2b) with these etale-origin witnesses: it gives the actual exchange isomorphism and its finite evaluations $\beta_n$. By [det-sp-tower-gluing], $G_f,G_{f'}$ also preserve $\mathcal C$, so $P_K,Q_K$ and the input of every counit below have the required uniform bounds.

source.place: (1), domain and restriction of the compactification exchange; (2), tower adjunction domains

proof.text:
The adjunction of [det-sp-tower-gluing] transposes $q_K:F_{f'}P_K\to v_\bullet^*K$ to the actual morphism $e_K=G_{f'}(q_K)\circ\eta_{f',P_K}$. Write $P(a)=u_\bullet^*G_f(a)$ for $a:K\to L$. Naturality of the exchange of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels] and of the counit gives
$$q_L\circ F_{f'}P(a)=v_\bullet^*(a)\circ q_K.$$
Naturality of the unit and functoriality now give
$$e_L\circ P(a)=G_{f'}(q_L\circ F_{f'}P(a))\circ\eta_{f',P_K}=G_{f'}v_\bullet^*(a)\circ e_K.$$
This proves tower naturality by an equality of actual tower morphisms.

source.place: (2), actual adjoint transpose and its naturality

proof.text:
Evaluate this composite with the derived evaluation functor of [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian](2). A functor preserves composition and carries the inverse of an isomorphism to the inverse of its image. Pullback evaluates levelwise by [lem-sp-ctf-tower-pullback-reconstruction], the exchange evaluates to $\beta_n$ by [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](2b), and the comparisons in [det-sp-tower-gluing](3) identify $G_f,G_{f'}$ and both adjunction maps with the finite ones. Substitution into the composite therefore gives exactly
$$\operatorname{ev}_n(e_K)=G_{f',n}(v_n^*\varepsilon_{f,n,K_n}\circ\beta_n(G_{f,n}K_n)^{-1})\circ\eta_{f',n,u_n^*G_{f,n}K_n}.$$
This is the specified finite counit transpose, not a choice of a lift from its evaluations.

source.place: (2), evaluation of exchange, counit, unit and transpose

proof.text:
Fix $1\le m\le n$, put $T=-\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m$ and $r=r^K_{n,m}$. The reduction formula in [det-sp-tower-gluing](3), with its coefficient comparison specified by [det-sp-reduction-exceptional], gives $r^{G_fK}=G_{f,m}(r)\circ c^f_{n,m}(K_n)$. Apply the pullback reduction identity of [lem-sp-ctf-tower-pullback-reconstruction] to obtain
$$r^P_{n,m}=u_m^*G_{f,m}(r)\circ u_m^*c^f_{n,m}(K_n).$$
For $Q$ apply the same gluing formula to the input $v_\bullet^*K$; its reduction is $v_m^*r$ by that pullback identity. This gives
$$r^Q_{n,m}=G_{f',m}(v_m^*r)\circ c^{f'}_{n,m}(v_n^*K_n).$$
All these equalities use the canonical tensor/pullback identifications of the cited statements.

source.place: (2), construction of both source and target reductions

proof.text:
The quotient $A_n\to A_m$ is among the finite commutative $\ell$-primary coefficient maps: [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels] identifies $A_n$ with $A_{E,en}$, including ramified $E$. By [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor](2), $TK_n$ is constructible finite-Tor with the same Tor interval as $K_n$, without flatness of $A_m$ over $A_n$. Thus the second identity of [det-sp-mixed-base-change] applies to $K_n$ and exactly the finite maps identified in Step 3:
$$c^{f'}_{n,m}(v_n^*K_n)\circ T(e_{n,K_n})=e_{m,TK_n}\circ u_m^*c^f_{n,m}(K_n).$$
The compactification is the same on the two coefficient levels and is pulled back for $f'$, as required by that identity.

source.place: (2), second mixed base-change identity at a possibly nonflat coefficient quotient

proof.text:
Precompose neither side of this identity; postcompose both sides by $G_{f',m}(v_m^*r)$ and use the formula for $r^Q$ in Step 4. This yields the first asserted equality. The finite version of the naturality calculation in Step 2 (using the finite adjunctions identified by [det-sp-tower-gluing](3)), applied to $r:TK_n\to K_m$, is
$$G_{f',m}(v_m^*r)\circ e_{m,TK_n}=e_{m,K_m}\circ u_m^*G_{f,m}(r).$$
Substitution followed by the formula for $r^P$ proves the second and third equalities. Reductions are natural in the entire input tower by [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian](3), and every exchange, unit, counit and coefficient comparison used above is natural. Hence the resulting equality is natural in $K$. No transition $r$ or mate $e_K$ was inverted; no normalization or flatness of the coefficient quotient was used.
